idea.body: A circle's circumference is 2 times pi times the radius, or pi times the diameter. An arc is a piece of the circumference. Its length is the same fraction of the circumference that its central angle is of 360 degrees. Both always stay an exact multiple of pi, never a decimal. A wheel with radius 6 centimeters has circumference 12 pi centimeters, since 2 times 6 is 12. An arc with a central angle of 90 degrees on that wheel is a quarter of the circle. Its length is a quarter of 12 pi, which is 3 pi centimeters.

figure.alt: A circle with center O, radii OA and OB, and the sector between them shaded.

workedExample.prompt: A dish antenna is a circle with radius 9 centimeters. Arc AB has a central angle of 120 degrees. As a multiple of pi, find the length of arc AB.
steps: The full circumference's multiple is 2 times 9, which is 18.
Arc AB is 120 out of 360 degrees, which is one third of the circle.

figure.alt: A circle with center O, radii OA and OB, and the sector between them shaded.

ways.name: The formula, then the fraction
ways.when: Use this any time you know the radius and a central angle.
steps: A wheel has radius 15 centimeters. Arc AB has a central angle of 72 degrees.
A circle's circumference is 2 times pi times the radius.
2 times 15 is 30, so the circumference is 30 pi centimeters.
An arc's length is the same fraction of the circumference as its angle is of 360 degrees.
72 out of 360 is 1/5, and 1/5 of 30 is 6, so arc AB is 6 pi centimeters.
ways.example: A circle has radius 15 centimeters. Arc AB has a central angle of 72 degrees. Find its length as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Forgetting to multiply by 2 and using just the radius as the circumference's multiple of pi.

figure.alt: A circle with center O, radii OA and OB, and the sector between them shaded.

frames.caption: Radius 15, arc AB has a 72 degree angle.
Radius 15 cm; arc angle is 72 degrees
An arc's fraction matches its angle / 360

ways.name: Diameter times pi directly
ways.when: Use this when the diameter is given straight across, instead of the radius.
steps: A dish antenna is a circle with diameter 22 centimeters.
A circle's circumference is also pi times its diameter, the distance straight across.
The diameter is already 22 centimeters, so there is no need to double a radius first.
Circumference is 22 pi centimeters, read straight from the diameter.
ways.example: A circle has diameter 22 centimeters. Find its circumference as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Doubling the diameter by mistake, treating it like a radius that still needs multiplying by 2.

figure.alt: A circle with a diameter drawn straight across through the center, from A to B.

frames.caption: Diameter is already 22; no radius needed

ways.name: The unit-degree rate
ways.when: Use this when several different arcs on the same circle are needed.
steps: A wheel has radius 6 centimeters. Arc AB has a central angle of 150 degrees.
Find how much arc length corresponds to just one degree: circumference divided by 360.
Circumference is 12 pi, so one degree is 12 pi divided by 360, which is pi/30.
Multiply that unit rate by the angle: 150 times pi/30 is 5 pi.
ways.example: A circle has radius 6 centimeters. Arc AB has a central angle of 150 degrees. Find its length as a multiple of pi.
ways.trap: Dividing by the angle instead of multiplying the per-degree rate by it.

The full circumference's multiple is 8 divided by 120/360, which is 8 times 360/120, or 24.
The radius is half the circumference's multiple: 24 divided by 2, which is 12 centimeters.
